items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: Willard Alexander was with MCA at that time.

ctx.x: MCA. Willard Alexander was with MCA at that time. That period is when we went to Chicago, took another flyer at studying music. For me it was a digression, very important. Before that we had begun making records. I guess they're the same size as a 33 now; they used to be small.

items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: the only income was an occasional weekend, which Wil- lard was forcing us to do... so we went out with pick up bands

ctx.x: the road at the end of '55 and the only-- now I had two kids ready to go to school, to higher education, and I had no means of putting them there.

A whole year I couldn't get any work in the studios in New York and the only income was an occasional weekend, which Wil- lard was forcing us to do, because we said we're not going out until--don't make us go out--so we went out with pick up bands, which was terrible.
You mean you'd go out to some town and get a bunch of locals?
